ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle C = 90^\circ$, $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$ and intersects $BC$ at point $D$. If $BD : CD = 3 : 2$ and the distance from point $D$ to $AB$ is 8, what is the length of $BC$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution}: Draw $DE\perp AB$ at point $E$ through point $D$,\\
since $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$, $\angle C=90^\circ$, and $DE\perp AB$,\\
it follows that $CD=DE=8$,\\
also, since $BD:CD=3:2$,\\
it follows that $BD=12$,\\
hence, $BC=BD+DC=\boxed{20}$.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, the base AB of triangle ABC is approximately horizontal, point C is above, and a right-angle mark is drawn at C, indicating that AC and CB are perpendicular. Point D is located on side CB, and segment AD connects from A to D. The four points A, B, C, and D are also marked in the figure; the perpendicular from D to AB is not directly drawn, but the problem gives this distance as 8. Reasoning: Because AD is the angle bisector of ∠BAC, and D is on the angle bisector AD, the perpendicular distances from point D to the two sides AB and AC of the angle are equal. The problem gives the distance from D to AB as 8, so the distance from D to AC is also 8. Also because in the figure D is on CB, and ∠C=90°, CB is perpendicular to AC, and therefore CD is also perpendicular to AC; thus CD is exactly the perpendicular distance from point D to AC, so CD=8. It is known that BD:CD=3:2, so BD=(3/2)×8=12. Finally BC=BD+CD=12+8=20.
